records.label: spacr.crop_loader#1
records.source: **WHAT IT IS FOR.** Every screen that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings screen had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. This module is the missing half: it turns a question about a plate into a stack of pixels, and it does it in two steps so a GUI can stay answerable between them.
records.context: **What it is for.** Every application view that shows objects has had its own way of finding them, and the Embeddings application view had none at all -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existed and nothing in ``spacr/`` called it, so the only route to a label-free vector was to open Python. This module is the missing half: it turns a question about a plate into a stack of pixels, and it does it in two steps so a GUI can stay answerable between them.
records.translation: **PARA QUE SERVE.** Cada tela que mostra objetos tinha sua própria maneira de encontrá-los, e a tela Embeddings não tinha nenhuma -- :meth:`spacr.qt.screens.embeddings.EmbeddingsScreen.set_crops` existia e nada em ``spacr/`` a chamava, então o único caminho para um vetor sem rótulos era abrir o Python. Este módulo é a metade que faltava: ele transforma uma pergunta sobre uma placa em uma pilha de pixels, e faz isso em duas etapas para que uma GUI possa continuar respondendo entre elas.
records.review_basis: MT draft edited in AI review

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#2
records.source: **PLANNING IS NOT LOADING, and that separation is the whole design.** :func:`plan_crops` asks the database or the folder *which objects match* and reads no pixels at all: a ``COUNT`` and a ``SELECT`` of identifiers, or one ``scandir``. It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand crops, so a screen can run it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that runs the second half on a worker thread gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.

It is milliseconds on a plate of sixty thousand extracted image regions, so a screen can execute it on a click and tell the user what they asked for before committing to reading any of it. :func:`load_crops` then reads the pixels in pages, reporting after each one. A caller that executes the second half on a background execution unit gets a progress number per page and a stop that takes effect within a page rather than at the end.
records.translation: **PLANEJAR NÃO É CARREGAR, e essa separação é todo o design.** :func:`plan_crops` pergunta ao banco de dados ou à pasta *quais objetos correspondem* e não lê pixel nenhum: um ``COUNT`` e um ``SELECT`` de identificadores, ou um único ``scandir``. Leva milissegundos em uma placa de sessenta mil recortes, então uma tela pode executá-lo com um clique e informar ao usuário o que ele pediu antes de se comprometer a ler qualquer parte. :func:`load_crops` então lê os pixels em páginas, reportando após cada uma. Um chamador que executa a segunda metade em uma thread de worker recebe um número de progresso por página e uma parada que tem efeito dentro de uma página, e não no final.

records.source: **A CAP IS PART OF THE ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE TO LOAD EVERYTHING.** Sixty thousand crops of 96x96x3 is 1.6 GB before a backbone has seen one of them, and a screen that tries it dies on a machine that could have embedded the first two thousand happily. So :attr:`CropQuery.limit` is a real default and the plan says what it left behind -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433" -- rather than quietly returning a subset that looks like the whole plate.
records.context: **A cap is part of the answer, not a failure to load everything.** Sixty thousand extracted image regions of 96x96x3 is 1.6 GB before a backbone has seen one of them, and a screen that tries it dies on a machine that could have embedded the first two thousand happily. So :attr:`CropQuery.limit` is a real default and the plan says what it left behind -- "the first 2,000 of 61,433" -- rather than quietly returning a subset that looks like the whole plate.
records.translation: **UM LIMITE FAZ PARTE DA RESPOSTA, NÃO É UMA FALHA EM CARREGAR TUDO.** Sessenta mil recortes de 96x96x3 somam 1.6 GB antes que um backbone tenha visto um único deles, e uma tela que tenta isso morre em uma máquina que teria gerado embeddings dos primeiros dois mil sem problema. Por isso :attr:`CropQuery.limit` é um padrão real e o plano diz o que deixou de fora -- "os primeiros 2,000 de 61,433" -- em vez de retornar silenciosamente um subconjunto que parece ser a placa inteira.

records.label: spacr.crop_loader#7
records.source: **AND A CAP IS NOT THE ONLY THING THAT REMOVES A ROW, SO IT IS COUNTED ON ITS OWN.** The merged route drops every row it cannot cut, and reporting that as a cap is the same sentence read backwards: a complete answer dressed as a subset, telling the user to raise a limit that never bit. So :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` and :attr:`CropPlan.count` are three numbers, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` is the gap between the first two and :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` the gap between the last two, and they reach the panel as separate clauses.

So :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` and :attr:`CropPlan.count` are three numbers, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` is the gap between the first two and :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` the gap between the last two, and they reach the panel as separate clauses.
records.translation: **E UM LIMITE NÃO É A ÚNICA COISA QUE REMOVE UMA LINHA, POR ISSO ELE É CONTADO À PARTE.** A rota mesclada descarta toda linha que não consegue recortar, e reportar isso como um limite é a mesma frase lida ao contrário: uma resposta completa disfarçada de subconjunto, dizendo ao usuário para aumentar um limite que nunca atuou. Por isso :attr:`CropPlan.matched`, :attr:`CropPlan.selected` e :attr:`CropPlan.count` são três números, :attr:`CropPlan.capped` é a diferença entre os dois primeiros e :attr:`CropPlan.dropped` a diferença entre os dois últimos, e eles chegam ao painel como orações separadas.

records.source: **THE PREDICATE IS SQL AND THE DATABASE IS OPENED READ-ONLY.** ``where`` is a fragment of the user's own query language against their own file; refusing it would mean inventing a worse one. It is spliced into a ``WHERE`` clause, so the connection is opened with ``readonly=True`` -- SQLite's ``query_only``, which refuses every write at the engine -- and a predicate carrying a statement separator is rejected before it is sent.

It is spliced into a ``WHERE`` clause, so the connection is opened with ``readonly=True`` -- SQLite's ``query_only``, which refuses every write at the engine -- and a predicate carrying a statement separator is rejected before it is sent.

records.label: spacr.diameter#6
records.source: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without eating the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test plate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. So the typical object is first located by the stained area it carries (the area-weighted median, which specks cannot move because they hold almost no area), everything narrower than :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` of it is dropped, and the characteristic size is the median of what remains. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.
records.context: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without eating the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu will happily bisect pure noise and hand back a confident-looking number. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is a lie) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test laboratory microplate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. So the typical object is first located by the stained area it carries (the area-weighted median, which specks cannot move because they hold almost no area), everything narrower than :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` of it is dropped, and the characteristic size is the median of what remains. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.
records.translation: 1. **Achatar.** Remove o ruído com uma gaussiana de 1 px e depois subtrai uma cópia fortemente suavizada (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) para eliminar gradientes de iluminação. O sigma é deliberadamente muito maior do que qualquer objeto plausível, para que o achatamento remova o vinheteamento sem consumir os objetos — a escolha oposta (uma esfera rolante estreita) encolhe justamente o que se tenta medir. 2. **Rejeitar ruído.** Compara a amplitude estrutural do plano achatado (p99 - p30) com a escala de ruído *no nível do pixel*, medida como ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` no plano bruto. Um plano de ruído puro pontua abaixo de 1; um plano com objetos reais pontua na casa das dezenas. Abaixo de ``min_snr`` o campo é descartado em vez de limiarizado, porque o Otsu divide ruído puro ao meio sem hesitar e devolve um número de aparência confiável. 3. **Limiarizar e rotular.** Otsu, preenchimento de buracos, rotulagem, descarte dos componentes que tocam a borda da imagem (truncados, então seu tamanho é enganoso) e dos componentes absurdos (diâmetro equivalente abaixo de ``min_object_diameter`` ou área acima de ``max_object_fraction`` do campo). Os tamanhos são diâmetros equivalentes, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Descartar pontinhos e depois tomar a mediana.** Uma marcação texturizada ou pontilhada (uma marcação mitocondrial de células, um marcador de parasita) se limiariza em alguns objetos inteiros mais centenas de pontinhos de 4-10 px, e uma mediana simples conta cada pontinho como um objeto: na própria placa de teste do spaCR, isso pôs a célula em 8 px e o patógeno em 11 px, contra 175 px e 32 px nas máscaras curadas, enquanto o núcleo, cuja marcação é sólida, saiu correto em 91 px. Por isso, o objeto típico é primeiro localizado pela área marcada que ele carrega (a mediana ponderada por área, que os pontinhos não conseguem deslocar porque quase não têm área), tudo o que for mais estreito que :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` dele é descartado, e o tamanho característico é a mediana do que resta. Componentes pequenos que juntos detêm :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` da área marcada ou mais são uma segunda população, não pontinhos, e permanecem. 5. **Verificação cruzada pela transformada de distância.** A etapa 3 tem um modo de falha dominante: uma monocamada confluente se funde em um único componente, esse componente toca a borda e é descartado, e a estimativa passa a ser calculada a partir dos detritos que sobraram — enviesada para **baixo**, e silenciosamente. Por isso, a transformada de distância euclidiana do primeiro plano (não preenchido) também é calculada, seus máximos locais são tomados como uma semente por objeto (duas passagens: uma passagem grosseira define o raio de supressão da passagem refinada), e um watershed sobre ``-EDT`` separa o primeiro plano fundido de volta em objetos cujos diâmetros equivalentes são medidos da mesma forma.
